chapter: Three Deuces and 52nd Street with Tatum
title: No help from Tatum or Slam; after-hours cutting contests
summary: They went their separate ways after work; he explains the friendly competition among pianists and how the trio played I Got Rhythm while talking baseball.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: If I had the knowledge to know that I have then or the know-how... If I had somebody to help me, I'd have been much better.
Did you try to get Tatum to help you out?

Well you see, no. See the only thing was once we finished the job it was straight home. Everybody went their separate ways. A lot of times we used to meet uptown, and sit at an after hours spot. And a lot of times he would be up there he'd be up there playing, you know

just sittin' up playing. And no time to ask nobody like them. Because all the other piano players were around trying to catch him off guard, or that type of thing. That's why you have to practice a lot or they step right on your nose. They're waitin' for you. But like they couldn't touch him... They'd keep 'em off him. I was... more competitive than it is now. Friendly, competitive, you know what I mean. Try to outplay each other. New guy would come into town, you know what I mean... think he smart... go up into a pool room and wash him away.
Did you try to get Slam Stewart to help son out with the arrangements.

No, like I said when we finished playing, everybody went his way... I guess they just figured, you know your instrument, you're a musician. It wasn't a matter of getting together unless you were a band, you know.
Yeah, yeah. Well we had to, we had a four voice thing goin' there, we had to. But I mean the three of us we just played, just sat down to play in a hell of a song way.
I Got Rhythm way up in tempo. And we'd talk about baseball or football. You know, like there was nothin happenin. Like we were holdin a conversation. On the bandstand.
